metadata.title: 21 Pots/Handi Pongal (Sweet Rice Dish) Making at TN House, Delhi I Rice (Curd +Tamarind + Sambar)
metadata.description:
On 14th January, this year Tamil Nadu House was transformed into a vibrant hub of festivities as we joined the Pongal celebrations. The venue was beautifully decorated with traditional motifs and bright colors setting the tone for the day. The highlight of the event was undoubtedly the mesmerizing performances by talented folk artists. They showcased traditional music and dance forms, bringing the essence of Tamil culture to life. 

Amidst the festivities, we had the pleasure of joining Rani Ji and Sangeeta Ji, who shared their invaluable insights into the festival's significance. They explained the symbolic aspects of Pongal and the importance of its different days. 

One of the most fascinating rituals we witnessed was the preparation of Pongal. The dish, cooked with care and devotion, was first offered to the gods as a mark of gratitude for nature’s bounty. It was then mixed with a larger batch of the same dish before being distributed to everyone present.

Thereafter we savoured a soul-nourishing spread that included curd rice, tamarind rice, sambar rice, sweet pongal and channa. Each dish reflected the rich flavours of Tamil Nadu and carried the warmth of the festival.

Pongal is more than just a celebration; it is a heartfelt tribute to nature, the hardworking farmers who sustain us, and the unity of the communities. This experience at Tamil Nadu House was a beautiful reminder of the values that bind us together.
